# redis_user (Resource)

The `redis_user` resource manages Redis users with ACL permissions (requires Redis 6.0+). This resource allows you to create, update, and delete Redis users with specific access controls as part of your Terraform infrastructure.

## Example Usage

### Basic Usage

```hcl
resource "redis_user" "app_user" {
  username = "app_user"
  password = "secure_password"
  enabled  = true
}
```

### Read-Only User

```hcl
resource "redis_user" "readonly_user" {
  username  = "readonly"
  password  = "password123"
  enabled   = true
  keys      = ["app:*", "cache:*"]
  commands  = ["+@read", "-@write", "-@admin"]
  channels  = ["notifications:*"]
}
```

### Admin User

```hcl
resource "redis_user" "admin_user" {
  username  = "admin"
  password  = "secure_admin_password"
  enabled   = true
  commands  = ["+@all"]
  keys      = ["*"]
}
```

### Complex ACL Configuration

```hcl
resource "redis_user" "service_user" {
  username       = "service_user"
  password       = "complex_password"
  enabled        = true
  keys           = ["service:*", "shared:*"]
  commands       = ["+@read", "+@write", "+@list", "+@set", "+@sorted_set", "+@hash", "-@dangerous"]
  channels       = ["events:*", "logs:*"]
  reset_keys     = true
  reset_channels = true
  reset_commands = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:

* `username` - (Required) The name of the Redis user. This is the identifier used to authenticate and apply ACL rules.
* `password` - (Optional) The password for the user. Set to empty string for passwordless authentication. Use `""` to explicitly set no password (NoPass).
* `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the user is enabled. Defaults to `true`. When set to `false`, the user cannot authenticate.
* `keys` - (Optional) List of key patterns the user can access (e.g., "cache:*"). Each pattern should follow Redis ACL key pattern syntax.
* `commands` - (Optional) List of commands or command categories the user can execute. Use prefix `+` to allow and `-` to disallow. Examples: `+@read`, `+get`, `-@dangerous`, `+@all`.
* `channels` - (Optional) List of Pub/Sub channel patterns the user can access. Each pattern follows Redis pattern matching syntax.
* `reset_keys` - (Optional) Whether to reset key permissions before applying new ones. Defaults to `false`.
* `reset_channels` - (Optional) Whether to reset channel permissions before applying new ones. Defaults to `false`.
* `reset_commands` - (Optional) Whether to reset command permissions before applying new ones. Defaults to `false`.

## Attribute Reference

In addition to all arguments above, the following attributes are exported:

* `id` - The Redis username (same as the `username` argument).

## Import

Redis user resources can be imported using the Redis username:

```bash
terraform import redis_user.example "my_username"
```

## Notes

* The `username` argument is marked as `ForceNew`, meaning that changing the username will destroy and recreate the resource.
* Redis ACL commands follow specific syntax:
  * Command categories use the `@` prefix: `+@read`, `-@write`
  * Individual commands: `+get`, `+set`, `-flushall`
  * Key patterns use glob-style syntax: `~cache:*`, `~user:*`
* When `reset_keys`, `reset_channels`, or `reset_commands` is set to `true`, the corresponding permissions will be completely reset before applying the new ones.
* This resource requires Redis 6.0 or later, which introduced the ACL system.
